evidence_quotes.quote: Moreover, the gap regarding non-connected households exceeds 365,000 inhabitants.

Nevertheless, the agency can act within the parameters of its rules, mainly through the design of tariff mechanisms that are capable of promoting the desired outcomes that highlight the importance of the proposed analysis.

Four policy alternatives were evaluated in order to reduce the non-connected household gap to sewage services taking into account: strong infrastructure diffusion (100%); advanced infrastructure diffusion (75%); intermediate infrastructure diffusion (50%) and do nothing (0%), which emphasize the tradeoff between investment allocation and subsidy policies.
To overcome this problem, the present paper provides an opportunity to observe an ex-ante regulatory impact assessment (RIA) as a policy tool in Brazil.
A conference panel and a web survey were used to obtain value functions and weights of the criteria.
For all hypothetical alternatives, the authors considered that the deployment cycle will occur within seven years (2016 to 2023).
This ex ante analysis allows a critical assessment of the household connection gap, although there is clear room for ex post analysis.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines the problem of household non-connection to public wastewater networks in four municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil (Belo Horizonte, Betim, Contagem, and Ribeirao das Neves).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (yes) because it examines Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) as a regulatory governance decision-making tool for the state water and wastewater regulator ARSAE and discusses mandatory connection statutes (Federal Law no. 11445/2007 art. 45; State Law no. 13317/1999 art. 48) and tariff mechanisms. Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading (no) because RIA is a general internal regulatory appraisal methodology rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household service access, and the four evaluated policy alternatives are generic hypothetical infrastructure-diffusion targets (100%, 75%, 50%, and 0% coverage of non-connected households) rather than specific eligibility, documentation, tariff, or enforcement rules. Note that plain_criterion2_decision remains exclude because the study also fails c3, c4, and c5 as an ex-ante simulation/MCDA exercise without empirical observation of household access outcomes.
criterion_notes.c3: No empirical evidence on service access outcomes. Although the authors use baseline secondary municipal statistics and elicit subjective criteria weights and value functions from a stakeholder focus group, conference panel, and web survey, the study is an ex-ante decision-modeling exercise projecting hypothetical scenarios for 2016-2023 / 2017-2026 (published in 2019), as the authors explicitly acknowledge in noting that this ex ante analysis leaves room for ex post analysis.
criterion_notes.c4: No empirically observed access outcome is reported. Reductions in non-connected households (100%, 75%, 50%, and 0%) and associated tariff/cost figures are stipulated or projected ex ante as hypothetical scenario parameters, while the actual evaluated output of the M-MACBETH model is the stakeholder-weighted policy attractiveness score and cost-benefit ranking of options for regulators.
criterion_notes.c5: While the ex-ante multi-criteria decision analysis (M-MACBETH) and cost-benefit projection methodology is identifiable, it is a prospective prescriptive decision-support simulation rather than an empirical study design measuring the relationship between an actual exposure and observed household or community access outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in English (eligible without translation).

study_design: Ex-ante regulatory impact assessment (RIA) using multi-criteria decision analysis (M-MACBETH), stakeholder preference elicitation (focus group, conference panel, web survey), and hypothetical cost-benefit projection
population_and_sample: Baseline municipal wastewater coverage population in Belo Horizonte, Betim, Contagem, and Ribeirao das Neves (BBCR), Minas Gerais (approx. 3.85 million inhabitants covered; 107,074 non-connected households / >365,000 inhabitants), plus a stakeholder focus group, conference panel, and web survey of ARSAE, academic, and local government participants
exposure: Hypothetical ex-ante regulatory policy options for wastewater infrastructure diffusion over 2016-2023 (2017-2026): strong infrastructure diffusion (100%), advanced infrastructure diffusion (75%), intermediate infrastructure diffusion (50%), and do nothing (0%)
outcome: M-MACBETH stakeholder-weighted policy attractiveness scores and cost-benefit frontier rankings across hypothetical scenarios (incorporating assumed/projected non-connected households, hospital stays/year, average tariffs, capex/opex, and sludge removed)
rationale: Excluded (E12: Wrong study design). This 2019 paper conducts an ex-ante Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (M-MACBETH) and prospective cost-benefit projections (modeled over 2016-2023 / 2017-2026) to help the Minas Gerais regulator (ARSAE) rank four hypothetical wastewater diffusion targets (100%, 75%, 50%, and 0% reductions in non-connected households). Household connection levels are assumed ex ante as scenario definitions rather than empirically observed outcomes, and primary data collection is restricted to stakeholder elicitation of subjective value functions and criteria weights. In addition, while the paper satisfies the plain reading of Criterion 2 by examining RIA as a regulatory governance tool, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading because the evaluated alternatives are generic infrastructure-diffusion targets rather than legal or administrative rules governing household access; because it lacks an empirical evaluation design measuring observed access outcomes, plain_criterion2_decision is also exclude.
